skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Let Codex use Google Antigravity CLI (agy) for repository exploration, bounded feature work, and project-scale implementation. Use when a Codex task benefits from delegated repository work while Codex retains diff review, verification, repair, and delivery assurance.
skill.summary: Delegate bounded repository work to AGY while Codex retains approval, review, verification, and delivery control.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives from dictionary-key checks, minified JSON Schemas, defensive path validation, documentation formatting, and bounded subprocess wrappers. Confirmed risks are the intentional AGY provider launch, driver-selected verifier execution, optional legacy shell verification, and externally transmitted repository content. No prompt injection attempt or concealed executable payload was found in the reviewed files. Static review was capped at 400/893 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 493 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Whole-worktree mode can expose all approved repository content to an external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Make scoped transmission the default, retain per-launch digest approval, and require a separate explicit override for whole-worktree transmission.

remediation.issue: Legacy verifier mode executes driver-selected text through Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Remove legacy shell verification where possible and require canonical argv verification for all routine checks.

remediation.issue: Static review was capped before all reported matches were presented.
remediation.suggestion: Complete a manual review of the remaining static matches before automatic publication.

content.value_statement: Large repository tasks can overwhelm one Codex session and weaken review discipline. This skill delegates bounded work to AGY while Codex controls approval, verification, and delivery.
actual_capabilities: Routes exploration, bounded implementation, and project-scale work through separate cycle budgets.
Creates branch-backed disposable worktrees and previews provider-readable content before dispatch.
Supports whole-worktree or digest-bound scoped transmission with explicit approval.
Preserves worker results, lifecycle state, and bounded repair cycles for review.
Validates result envelopes and binds driver-owned verification before finalization.
Provides compatibility checks, model selection records, benchmarks, and usage reports.
limitations: Requires Codex, Bash, Python 3, Git, AGY, and provider access for live dispatch.
Claude and Claude Code hosts are not supported, despite provider model names that may contain Claude.
The worktree and scoped staging controls are not filesystem or network sandboxes.
Worker output remains untrusted until Codex reviews the diff and runs relevant checks.

use_cases.title: Explore an unfamiliar repository

use_cases.title: Coordinate project-scale delivery

best_practices: Prefer scoped transmission and review every selected file before approving a provider launch.
Keep secrets, credentials, private files, raw logs, and controller state outside approved provider content.
Inspect candidate bytes and run driver-owned checks before assigning any final assurance label.
anti_patterns: Do not treat installation, preview, or offline readiness as provider-transmission approval.
Do not execute commands or tests reported by the worker envelope.
Do not claim correctness, security, or completion from provider success alone.

faq.question: What does this skill delegate?
faq.answer: It delegates repository exploration, bounded implementation, and project work to AGY while Codex keeps acceptance authority.

faq.question: Does it send repository content to an external provider?
faq.answer: Yes. Approved content may be sent through AGY to Google or Gemini provider services.

faq.question: Can I limit what the provider reads?
faq.answer: Yes. Scoped transmission stages reviewed entries and binds their content digest, but it is not a complete sandbox.

faq.question: Does it support Claude or Claude Code hosts?
faq.answer: No. The package requires an OpenAI Codex host, even when a provider model name contains Claude.

faq.question: Does a successful worker run prove the change is correct?
faq.answer: No. Codex must inspect the diff and run relevant driver-owned verification before acceptance.

faq.question: What local tools are required?
faq.answer: The live workflow requires Codex, Bash, Python 3, Git, AGY, and working provider access.
